decisions.reason: The citrus harvesting crate extends the firm's established agricultural crate know-how, so it can interpret field feedback and refine the design in-house, although its niche, seasonal market makes it somewhat more exposed than core lines.

The foldable large container sits at the heart of the firm's returnable packaging expertise, held a dedicated page in both observed years, and serves automotive and industrial customers whose needs engineering can absorb and turn into improvements.
A stackable plastic crate builds directly on the firm's deepest injection-moulding and crate knowledge, making it easy to assimilate market feedback and keep it as a staple of the range.
The medium-duty rackable pallet is closely related to the firm's existing pallet engineering, so performance data from customers and pooling organisations can be readily interpreted and applied.

The spill-retention pallet relies on related moulding competence but serves a more specialised safety and regulatory niche where the firm's knowledge base is thinner, and its slide from a dedicated page to a mention signals reduced emphasis, yet it is still likely retained.

The pallet with load retainers is an incremental variant of core pallet technology that the firm can improve through in-house engineering, though its lower visibility in 2019 suggests a modest risk of being folded into the standard range.
